mathematicalFindings: A cube of edge a can indeed be partitioned into three congruent oblique square pyramids: choose one common cube vertex as apex and use the three square faces not incident to that vertex as bases. Their union is the cube; cyclic permutation of coordinate directions maps one pyramid to another.
Each such pyramid has square base area a^2 and perpendicular height a. Thus the special cube decomposition yields V=a^3/3=(1/3)Gh without integration.

The isolated solids each depict one apex and a quadrilateral base, with appropriate dashed hidden edges. The apex is displaced above a base vertex, as required by the oblique construction; the image does not falsely label these as regular/central pyramids.
The solids are schematic perspective views, not dimensioned technical drawings. No label contradicts the square-base/height interpretation.
The display at 360 px keeps the cube, three colored pyramids, a, G=a^2, h=a and V=(1/3)Gh readable. The small green phrase is secondary.
